result.gate: Phase 0 gate is 'a second agent reading cold agrees on at least 55 of 60'. 59/60 cold. PASS.

disagreements.verdict: genuine ambiguity, not a bad key
disagreements.why: The pool held both m_hills ('User walks in the hills most weekends when the weather holds') and m_peaks ('Easter weekends are usually spent in the Peak District'). 'Where' asks for a place and m_peaks is the only named place, so it reads as the better answer to the literal question; m_hills is the better answer to the habit. Two defensible answers in one pool.
disagreements.fix: Rewrote the case rather than moving the key: dropped m_peaks from b22's pool (10 -> 9 memories, still inside the 8-12 rule) and added a note recording why. The key stays m_hills, which is the plan's own worked example of a group B case ('hiking' -> 'walks in the hills'), so the B intent is preserved exactly. With m_peaks gone the case has one answer and my cold choice and the key now coincide.

corrections_to_test_recall: b22: removed pool member m_peaks; added a 'note' field explaining the removal. No key was changed, no case dropped, no other case touched.

final_tests.command: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests  (run from smCLM_02/)
final_tests.skips: The 4 skips are the leak checks and the ideas-inventory check; data/sentences.jsonl, data/tags.jsonl and ideas.json arrive in phases 1-2, and the tests are written to skip until then. All 10 fixture checks ran and passed.

unresolved_concerns: b34 'How do I usually travel to work?' -> m_cycle. I picked this cold and it matches the key, but 'cycles to the office when it is dry' is conditional, so 'usually' is a slight stretch. Left as is; worth watching if a ranker misses it.

c54 'Who do I call when the heating is off?' -> m_boiler (Hargreaves). I picked this cold and it matches the key. m_landlord ('slow about repairs') is still arguably defensible, and b32/c51 establish the user rents. Not changed, because the query asks who to call about heating and Hargreaves is the only heating contractor named, but it is the second-softest case in the set.
b26 'Who is my four-legged friend?' and b40 both lean on Biscuit appearing in two memories (m_dog, m_vet). The split is clean (animal vs venue) but the two cases are not independent.

The gate wording says a reviewer works 'without seeing the answer key'. I never opened test_recall.json before writing my choices, but the blind file was prepared by someone else, so the isolation is only as good as that extraction. The blind file does carry all 60 ids, queries and pools verbatim, which I confirmed after the fact.
Scope note: only smCLM_02/phase0_review.json and the one b22 edit in smCLM_02/test_recall.json were written. No model endpoint was called and no Phase 1 work started.
